scope: Review round 1 (eba4fa9c), narrowed by the INFRA-115 architect (envoy 3d4d8ca0) to the reviewer's three findings; the two Minor points and the reviewer's one-SQL-definition note go on the Fast-follow line. Main not merged: GitHub reports MERGEABLE.
answersReview: Thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6wduPX (clock beats before the broker serves): the serving clock is built and started beside srv.Serve, after close(serveStarted), still on serving. Fixed in 301addfd; TestABrokerThatDiesBeforeServingRecordsNoServingBeat.

Thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6wduPg (a beat has no deadline; a held lock stalls it silently and the guard fails open): each beat runs under context.WithTimeout(Interval) with lock_timeout, statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout set to Interval for its transaction, and the WARN carries timed_out. A deadline alone cannot keep the guard off while one row is held, so migration 0019 now keeps one row per broker process (process, last_serving_at, not_serving_after; no seed): a beat upserts only its own row when no gap exists, and only a beat that finds a gap takes pg_advisory_xact_lock to give the time back once; enrollment_lease_live reads the latest row. Fixed in 301addfd; TestAHeldServingLockFailsTheBeatAndAnotherBrokerKeepsTheGuardOff.

Thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6wduPo (no Contract change census for the config refusal): the PR body now carries a Contract change census with both searches, every hit and its disposition, and the rollout line.

trickyParts: The per-process row is what lets another broker keep the guard off while one row is held: with a single row no broker can record that it serves while any transaction holds it.
Exactly-once give-back: only a beat whose fast upsert found a gap takes the advisory lock, re-reads the latest row with a fresh statement, and gives back; a second waiter then finds no gap.
